title: design-ledger run manifest
description: The structured account a run writes of the objects it produced: findings, assumptions, gates, decisions, recommendations, artifacts. The manifest is the run's own testimony. Substrate-measured facts (cost, tokens, exit status) and human gate answers keep their own authority; the board joins them to this file rather than trusting the run to assert them. Design rationale and emission contract: docs/run-manifest.md.

limits.description: What this run could not see, verify, or emit. Successor of the facts files' honesty notes. An empty or missing list claims nothing.

id.description: Slug identifier, unique within its collection, stable across re-renders of the same run. Observed in the wild as slugs like finding-dup-charge and roots-club-research-scope.

workflow.description: Practice workflow name, e.g. design-qa, ux-review, pmf-review, research-brief.

skill_id.description: Skill id as the substrate lists it, e.g. pk-design-qa.

engine.description: Agent runtime that executed the run, e.g. claude-code.

status.description: completed: deliverable written, no blocking gate open. gated: stopped at a blocking gate, deliverable withheld. failed: run ended without meeting its contract.

session_id.description: Substrate session identifier, the board's join key to daemon and log data.

log.description: Basename of the saved SSE log this run corresponds to. Join hint added at harvest time.

project.description: Substrate project identifier — the basename of the workspace directory. The write path (docs/write-path.md) uses it to target the continuation.

resumes.description: Run id this run resumed. A gated run and its resumption are two manifests linked by this field.

provenance.description: emitted: written by the run itself. backfilled: reconstructed later from session records; the board must label it as such.

path.description: Path relative to the run workspace. Absolute paths, home paths, and parent traversal are rejected: manifests travel, machine paths must not.

kind.description: Free string, e.g. report, image, data.

statement.description: The claim, one sentence, as it appears in the deliverable.

basis.description: Evidence basis as the design-qa runs of 2026-08-31 emitted it: reported (observed or stated by a source), derived (inferred from evidence), unverified. Optional because other workflows (ux-review, observed the same day) emit findings without a basis column; a backfill omits what the run did not label.

location.description: Where in the flow or surface, e.g. 'step 3, payment'.

basis.description: Why it is assumed and what, if anything, it leans on.

kind.description: Free string, e.g. uncertainty, taste, tradeoff, stop-ship, scope, conflict.

blocking.description: A blocking gate withholds the deliverable until answered (the research-brief pattern). A checkpoint gate rides with a delivered artifact and blocks the next decision instead (the design-qa and ux-review pattern); set blocking false for those. Defaults to true: an unmarked open gate reads as work stopped.

decision.description: Id of the decision that answered this gate. Required when state is answered.

type.description: Input type as the substrate rendered it, e.g. radio.

default.description: Default value: a string for single-choice questions, an array of strings for multi-select. Observed both shapes on 2026-08-31.

answer.description: Human-readable answer as given, e.g. 'Option A — confidence, narrow scope'.

answers.description: Per-question values when captured, keyed by question id.

via.description: Surface the answer came from, e.g. 'Cowork session'.

declared_by.description: run: the run's own unverified self-check. session-record: checked by a human or session tooling after the fact.

tags.description: The run's own vocabulary, carried verbatim without normalization, e.g. the pmf-review evidence labels strong/partial or the research-brief tags measured/calculated.
